newsitem.title: IRAQ: 300,000 tonnes of grains arrive in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: 300,000 tonnes of grains arrive in Iraq.

text.p: More than 300,000 tonnes of wheat and rice have arrived in Iraq under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations and stocks of other foodstuffs are piling up, a U.N. official said on Monday.

Eric Falt, spokesman for Iraq's U.N. coordinator, said wheat flour was now being distributed in Iraq including the three Kurdish provinces in the north currently outside the control of the central government in Baghdad.

Falt said the distribution in Kurdish provinces was carried out by U.N. World Food Programme. In other parts of Iraq the trade ministry and its retail agents did the distribution under monitoring by more than 120 U.N. observers.

Eric said in total 13 ships have docked at port of Umm Qasr in southern Iraq carrying items under the deal. "We have passed the mark of 100 approved contracts and foodstuffs from 20 of them are pouring into Iraq," he said.
He said he expected the sanctions-hit Iraqis to be able soon to get rations of rice, salt, pulses, cooking oil, tea, soap and detergent powder.
The first Iraq-bound shipment of food to be sent through Jordan under the deal docked at the Jordanian Sea port of Aqaba on Friday.
Eric said the 52,500 tonnes of wheat in the vessel were now reaching Iraq in a fleet of trucks.
Another 150,000 tonnes of French wheat purchased by Iraq from L. Dreyfus are expected to be discharged in Aqaba in three shipments over the coming few months.
Eric said about 50 percent of the approved contracts were related to the purchase of medical supplies. But he said no medicine had reached Iraq yet.

Cooking oil from Malaysia was arriving at Umm Qasar, Eric said. Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi visited Baghdad recently seeking sales under the oil deal and a role in developing Iraqi oilfields.

Iraq relies on imports of Malaysian cooking oil. It has allocated $111 million to buy cooking oil out of $1.3 billion it expects to get each six months from the oil deal allowed by the United Nations.
Iraq is under U.N. trade sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait but the oil-for-food deal is exempt from trade curbs.
